title: Canary Ops Sprint Template and Steward Brief
body:
Purpose

A compact, operational sprint template for running cross-functional canary activations (small-batch LLM features). Designed for 1–2 week ops sprints where a steward coordinates telemetry, safety gates, and stakeholder comms. Not a formal playbook — this is a working brief for stewards and oncall owners to run safe, observable micro-activations.

Scope
- Applies to: new model variants, routing changes, latency-optimized quantized builds, and small UX experiments that depend on runtime fallbacks.
- Not for: broad product launches or infra-only maintenance windows.

Sprint rhythm (recommended)
- Day -7: Hypothesis + minimal acceptance criteria logged (owner, WHY, success metric). Link to ticket.
- Day -5: Telemetry stubbed into dashboards (latency, p50/p95, token costs, error-rate, fallback-rate, quality delta by cohort).
- Day -3: Dry run on staging with synthetic traffic; run chaos probes (rate spikes, cold-cache).
- Day 0: Canary activation (1% -> 5% over 2h -> 20% over 8h) using cohort slices.
- Day 1–3: Observation window (collect stability + quality signals).
- End of sprint: Decision meeting: promote / iterate / rollback. Capture artifacts and short postmortem.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Steward (primary): runs the sprint, owns go/no-go cadence, runs comms playbook.
- Observability lead: owns dashboards and extraction of signal drift.
- Safety reviewer: runs content/regression checks and monitors flagged cohorts.
- Backend owner: rollback path, throttles, routing config.
- Customer success (if applicable): surfaces customer contracts that must be honored before promotion.

Pre-activation checklist (quick)
- Feature flag created and validated in staging.
- Canary cohorts defined (size, targeting, exclusion list).
- Dashboard links and runbooks in the activation ticket.
- Alert thresholds set (latency spike, error surge, fallback > 2x baseline, QA score drop > 5 points).
- Rollback automation tested in staging (toggle and traffic rebalancer).
- Communication templates drafted (see below).

Activation procedure (operational script)
1) 00:00 — Flip canary to 1% for cohort A. Notify stakeholders channel (ops-rollouts) with baseline numbers.
2) +60m — Check latency/error/fallback windows; manual spot-check 10 random responses.
3) If stable, scale to 5% and expand cohort B.
4) After 4–8h of stability, scale to 20% but limit request burst for first hour.
5) If any alert breaches threshold, run immediate mitigation (pin to previous model variant, enable fallback routing, or scale down to 0.1%).

Primary telemetry & guardrails (suggested metrics)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for gen & embed endpoints
- Errors: 5xx, 4xx ramp, rate-limited responses
- Fallback-rate: fraction of requests that hit secondary model/path
- Cost per 1k tokens (delta vs baseline)
- Quality metrics: eval set BLEU/ROUGE or internal QA score; prompt-specific hallucination signal if available
- User impact: task completion or click-through where applicable

Decision matrix (promote / iterate / rollback)
- Promote if: no alerts, quality delta <= +1% regression, latency within SLA, cost delta acceptable to product owner.
- Iterate if: marginal regressions (quality 1–5%) and no systemic errors — run targeted tests + model tweaks.
- Rollback if: critical alerts (latency > 2x SLO, error spike, safety incidents) or quality regression > 5% on core prompts.

Communication templates (short)
- Pre-activation: "Canary start: %feature% at 1% for cohort A. Steward: @Asha. Watch: latency p95, fallback-rate. Dash: <link>."
- Escalation: "URGENT: Canary %feature% breaching %metric% at %value%. Pausing rollout. Steward action: rollback initiated. Details: <link>."
- Post: "Canary complete: outcome=%promote/iterate/rollback%. Key signals: latency Δ, QA Δ, cost Δ. Follow-ups: owner list and tickets."

Templates & artifacts to attach to sprint ticket
- Target cohort definition (CSV sample of inclusion/exclusion)
- Dashboard links (prod + staging)
- Synthetic test harness commands + seed inputs
- Quick rollback cheat commands

Open questions / TODOs
- Which QA eval set becomes canonical for small releases? (Product decision required)
- Add automatic drift detection for semantics (not only token-level QA) — assign to Observability.
- Should we standardize 4-hour vs 8-hour hold windows for LLM features? Consensus needed.

After-action artifacts (post-sprint)
- Short postmortem (2–3 bullets) capturing why decision selected, any infra work needed, and follow-up tickets.
- Cost reconciliation: delta notes and estimate of month-over-month impact.
- Updated onboarding notes for the steward rotation calendar.

Appendix: steward quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Ticket linked to experiment doc + owner
- [ ] Dashboards up (links present)
- [ ] Cohort CSV uploaded
- [ ] Rollback tested in staging
- [ ] Comms templates ready
- [ ] Oncall informed and pager stack assigned

Notes to self (working):
- Keep this brief; teams want a single-sheet action plan during activation.
- Push for one canonical QA evalset next quarter.

References
- Related tickets: JIRA-LLM-876 (canary infra), CONFLUENCE-1234 (rollout taxonomy)
- Example runbook: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts

-- end of brief --
